0d31b5cf4345.source:
flowchart TD R1["Round 1: fit h₁ to equally-weighted data
upweight misclassified ○"] --> R2["Round 2: fit h₂ to reweighted data
upweight newly-misclassified ●"] R2 --> R3["Round 3: fit h₃ to reweighted data"] R3 --> FINAL["Final ensemble:
F = α₁h₁ + α₂h₂ + α₃h₃
(weighted vote)"]
0d31b5cf4345.caption: AdaBoost refits a weak classifier after increasing the weights of previously misclassified observations, then combines the classifiers by weighted voting.
0d31b5cf4345.alt: Three AdaBoost rounds reweight misclassified observations before fitting the next weak classifier, followed by a weighted ensemble vote.

0e5222fb5c6c.source:
flowchart TD
    A[Fit model] --> B[Did risk flatten?]
    B --> C[Did validation risk choose a reasonable mstop?]
    C --> D[Are residuals structured?]
    D --> E[Do intervals or probabilities calibrate?]
    E --> F[Interpret or revise model]
0e5222fb5c6c.caption: Diagnosis checks training-risk stabilization, validation-based stopping, residual structure, and predictive calibration before interpretation.
0e5222fb5c6c.alt: Diagnostic workflow from model fit through risk, stopping iteration, residual, and calibration checks to interpretation or model revision.

1415e9049cb4.source:
flowchart TD X["covariates x"] --> LP["linear predictor
η = xTβ"] LP --> LINK["link function
g(μ) = η"] LINK --> MEAN["mean
μ = g⁻¹(η)"] MEAN --> DIST["distribution
ExpFam(μ, φ)"] DIST --> Y["response y"]
1415e9049cb4.caption: A generalized linear model maps covariates to a linear predictor, transforms it to a conditional mean through the inverse link, and specifies a response distribution.
1415e9049cb4.alt: Generalized linear model pipeline from covariates through the linear predictor and link to the conditional mean and response distribution.

15fd1522d4b3.source:
flowchart TD CYC["Cycle t"] subgraph UPD[" "] direction LR MU["Update μ
penalized IRLS for η_μ
(σ, ν held)"] --> SIG["Update σ
penalized IRLS for η_σ
(μ updated, ν held)"] --> NU["Update ν
penalized IRLS for η_ν
(μ, σ updated)"] end CHK{"deviance change < ε ?"} STOP["converged — stop"] CYC --> UPD --> CHK CHK -- no --> CYC CHK -- yes --> STOP
15fd1522d4b3.caption: GAMLSS backfitting updates distribution parameters sequentially with the latest values of the other parameters and stops when deviance stabilizes.
15fd1522d4b3.alt: Cyclic GAMLSS updates for location, scale, and shape followed by a global-deviance convergence check.

232bbeb3595e.source:
flowchart TD U["u
(pseudo-residual)"] --> S["scan all splits
(j, s) across columns"] S --> BEST["best stump
var j*, split s*"] BEST --> ENC["β = [j*, s*, μ_L, μ_R]
4 numbers"] ENC --> PRED["predict: μ_L if x[j*] ≤ s* else μ_R"]
232bbeb3595e.caption: A tree base learner scans candidate splits, stores the winning split and node means, and replays that compact representation during prediction.
232bbeb3595e.alt: Tree base-learner pipeline from pseudo-residuals through split search and compact coefficient encoding to prediction.

247f281a84cc.source:
flowchart TD A["1. Current fit:
f⁽ᵐ⁻¹⁾(xᵢ) — additive predictor so far"] A --> B["2. Residuals:
uᵢ = yᵢ − f⁽ᵐ⁻¹⁾(xᵢ) = negative gradient"] B --> C["3. Fit ALL base learners to u:
ĝ₁ = linear fit on x₁
ĝ₂ = spline fit on x₂
..."] C --> D["4. Select best:
j* = argminⱼ Σᵢ(uᵢ − ĝⱼ)²"] D --> E["5. Update:
f⁽ᵐ⁾ = f⁽ᵐ⁻¹⁾ + ν · ĝⱼ*"] E -->|repeat| A
247f281a84cc.caption: An L2Boosting iteration computes residuals, fits every candidate learner, selects the minimum-SSE fit, and adds a shrunken update.
247f281a84cc.alt: Five-step L2Boosting cycle from the current fit through residual calculation, fitting all learners, minimum-SSE selection, and a shrunken update.

2d1dde2fcdb5.source:
flowchart TD
    A["Start at β⁰"] -->|"pick best coordinate"| B["Update β₁"]
    B -->|"pick best coordinate"| C["Update β₂"]
    C -->|"pick best coordinate"| D["Update β₁"]
    D -->|"..."| E["Converge at β*"]
    style A fill:#e8e8e8
    style E fill:#d4edda
2d1dde2fcdb5.caption: Greedy coordinate descent repeatedly evaluates candidate coordinates and updates the direction that most reduces the objective.
2d1dde2fcdb5.alt: Path from an initial coefficient vector to the optimum through successive updates of the best coordinate.

320b566771c2.source:
flowchart LR
    A[fit] --> B[cvrisk]
    B --> C[optimal mstop]
    C --> D[with_mstop]
    D --> E[coef / selected]
    D --> F[predict]
    D --> G[diagnostics]
320b566771c2.caption: Cross-validation selects the stopping iteration; the truncated path then supplies coefficients, predictions, and diagnostics.
320b566771c2.alt: Quickstart workflow from fitting and cross-validation through optimal stopping and path truncation to model summaries and diagnostics.

351c07eaa8d0.source:
flowchart LR
    A["Fitted model"] --> B["mstop"]
    A --> C["risk_"]
    A --> D["selected"]
    A --> E["coef"]
    A --> F["predict"]
    A --> G["diagnostics"]
    B --> H["with_mstop(k) or model[:k]"]
    D --> I["which base learner won each step"]
    E --> J["aggregated coefficients or per-step paths"]
    F --> K["link, response, class, partial contribution"]
    G --> L["residuals, calibration, intervals, PIT, Q-stats"]
351c07eaa8d0.caption: The fitted-model interface exposes stopping, risk, selected learners, coefficients, predictions, and diagnostics from one stored boosting path.
351c07eaa8d0.alt: Methods and attributes of a fitted model, including path truncation, learner selection, coefficient aggregation, prediction types, and diagnostics.

353bc6995d70.source:
flowchart TD subgraph PREP["prepare_* (once, before the loop)"] P1["allocate f, u (length n)"] P2["allocate rhs_buf, beta_buf, pred_buf (max p_j)"] P3["factorise Gram per learner"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 end subgraph LOOP["hot loop — m = 1 .. mstop"] L1["ngradient_and_risk writes into u"] L2["learner[j].fit_step_ref(u, ..., rhs_buf, beta_buf, pred_buf)
borrows the same 3 buffers per learner"] L3["select j* ; f += nu * pred_buf"] L1 --> L2 --> L3 end PREP -.->|"zero alloc"| LOOP style LOOP fill:#d4edda
353bc6995d70.caption: Learner preparation allocates and factorizes once; each boosting iteration reuses the same buffers for gradient computation, learner fitting, and the selected update.
353bc6995d70.alt: Two-stage engine design: one-time allocation and Gram factorization followed by an allocation-free boosting loop that reuses scratch buffers.

3c2d995fa6eb.source:
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as User
    participant F as Front end
    participant B as Binding
    participant C as Core
    participant L as Learner

    U->>F: gamboost(formula, data)
    F->>F: parse formula
    F->>F: one record per learner
    F->>B: fit specs
    B->>C: fit_with(family)
    C->>L: prepare(weights)
    L-->>C: learner + recipe
    loop m = 1 .. mstop
        C->>C: negative gradient
        C->>L: fit_step
        L-->>C: beta, pred, sse
        C->>C: select, update f
    end
    C-->>B: path
    B-->>F: path + store
    F-->>U: fitted model
3c2d995fa6eb.caption: Python and R front ends prepare learners, call the shared Rust engine, and reconstruct a fitted model from the returned boosting path.
3c2d995fa6eb.alt: Sequence from user code through the front end and language binding to learner preparation and the iterative Rust boosting engine, followed by reconstruction of the fitted model.

3f44fb1b8530.source:
flowchart LR
    subgraph S1[" "]
        direction TB
        A[Applied question] --> B[Choose family]
        B --> C[Choose base learners]
        C --> D[Fit long path]
    end
    subgraph S2[" "]
        direction TB
        E[Tune or slice mstop] --> F[Diagnose]
        F --> G[Interpret]
        G --> H[Report limitations]
    end
    D --> E
3f44fb1b8530.caption: An applied analysis proceeds from the scientific question through family and learner choices, path fitting, tuning, diagnosis, interpretation, and limitations.
3f44fb1b8530.alt: End-to-end case-study workflow from the applied question to a fitted and tuned model, diagnostics, interpretation, and reporting limitations.

409a1c730568.source:
flowchart TD subgraph MU["Parameter μ (η₁)"] direction TB MBL["base learners: bols(x₁), bbs(x₂)"] MUG["u_μ = −∂R/∂η_μ"] MUP["fit & select → update η_μ += ν·ĝ"] MBL --> MUG --> MUP end subgraph SIG["Parameter σ (η₂)"] direction TB SBL["base learners: bbs(x₂), bols(x₃)"] SUG["u_σ = −∂R/∂η_σ"] SUP["fit & select → update η_σ += ν·ĝ"] SBL --> SUG --> SUP end JOINT["Joint risk:
R(η₁,...,η_K) = −Σ log d(y | θ)"] JOINT --> MU JOINT --> SIG
409a1c730568.caption: Distributional boosting maintains separate additive predictors and learner-selection paths for each distribution parameter while optimizing a joint risk.
409a1c730568.alt: A joint negative log-likelihood supplies parameter-specific gradients to separate location and scale learner sets and predictors.

59cc9af5f0a8.source:
flowchart TD A["Forward stagewise
(small steps, no re-fit)"] --> D["Lasso path
(ℓ₁-regularized)"] B["L2Boosting
(ν → 0 limit)"] --> D C["Least angle regression (LARS)
(infinitesimal angle steps)"] --> D
59cc9af5f0a8.caption: For orthogonal designs and infinitesimal step sizes, forward stagewise regression, L2Boosting, and LARS trace the lasso coefficient path.
59cc9af5f0a8.alt: Forward stagewise regression, infinitesimal-step L2Boosting, and least angle regression converge to the same lasso path under orthogonality.

5ca15c1707cb.source:
flowchart LR MB["Model-based boosting
specified additive effects
shrinkage and early stopping"] LASSO["Lasso / elastic net
fixed design columns
global ℓ₁ / ℓ₂ penalty"] RF["Random forest
randomized trees
regularization by averaging"] GB["Tree gradient boosting
sequential fitted trees
depth, shrinkage, early stopping"]
5ca15c1707cb.caption: Model-based boosting, penalized regression, random forests, and tree boosting differ in their candidate components and regularization mechanisms.
5ca15c1707cb.alt: Comparison of model-based boosting with lasso or elastic net, random forests, and tree gradient boosting.

60155561883b.source:
flowchart LR
    A[Formula term or learners list] --> B[Name and position]
    C[Programmatic learner] --> D[Matrix payload]
    B --> E[gamboost learners=...]
    D --> E
    E --> F[Rust learner setup]
60155561883b.caption: Formula terms and programmatic learner specifications are normalized before the Rust core prepares their design and penalty structures.
60155561883b.alt: Formula and programmatic learner inputs converge at the gamboost learner interface and then enter Rust learner setup.

932dc08737ca.source:
flowchart TD Y["Y | X ~ D( θ₁(X), θ₂(X), ..., θ_K(X) )
all parameters modelled"] T1["g₁(θ₁) = η₁
f₁(x)'s"] T2["g₂(θ₂) = η₂
f₂(x)'s"] TK["g_K(θ_K) = η_K
f_K(x)'s"] Y --> T1 Y --> T2 Y --> TK subgraph EX ["Examples"] GL["GaussianLSS (K=2)
μ = f₁(x₁) + f₂(x₂)
σ = f₃(x₁) + f₄(x₃)"] ST["StudentTLSS (K=3)
μ, σ, ν all modelled
(tail heaviness varies with X)"] end
932dc08737ca.caption: GAMLSS assigns a separate additive predictor and link function to every modeled distribution parameter.
932dc08737ca.alt: A response distribution whose location, scale, and shape parameters each have their own covariate-dependent additive predictor.

a0db614dc3de.source:
flowchart TD ETA["η_k
(predictor scale)"] THETA["θ_k = g_k⁻¹(η_k)
(parameter scale)"] SK["score on predictor scale
s_k = (∂log d/∂θ_k) / g'_k(θ_k)"] D["score in natural parameterisation
∂log d/∂θ_k"] ETA -->|"∂θ_k/∂η_k = 1 / g'_k(θ_k)"| THETA THETA --- D D --- SK SK -.->|"rescaled by link derivative"| ETA
a0db614dc3de.caption: The chain rule converts a likelihood score on the distribution-parameter scale to the additive-predictor scale through the inverse-link derivative.
a0db614dc3de.alt: Relationship among predictor scale, parameter scale, the natural-parameter likelihood score, and the score rescaled by the link derivative.

a148e917bcbf.source:
flowchart TD A["p candidate predictors
x₀, x₁, ..., x₁₉"] --> B["iteration 1:
pick best column
update its coefficient
by ν·cor(y, xⱼ)"] B --> C["iteration 2:
recompute residuals
pick best column"] C --> D["... continued ..."] D --> E["sparse final model
3 of 20 coefficients ≠ 0"]
a148e917bcbf.caption: `glmboost` repeatedly recomputes residuals, selects one predictor, and adds a shrunken coefficient update, producing a sparse stopped model.
a148e917bcbf.alt: Component-wise linear boosting selects one of many predictors at each iteration and accumulates small coefficient updates in a sparse model.

a553f980afdf.source:
flowchart LR
    A[Boosting path] --> B[Selection path]
    A --> C[Coefficient path]
    A --> D[Risk / AIC path]
    A --> E[Residuals]
    B --> F[Variable importance]
    C --> G[Coefficient summaries]
    D --> H[mstop choice]
    E --> I[Diagnostics]
a553f980afdf.caption: A fitted boosting path supports selection, coefficient, risk, and residual summaries that feed interpretation, stopping, and diagnostic procedures.
a553f980afdf.alt: Branches from the boosting path to selection, coefficients, risk or AIC, and residuals, then to importance, summaries, stopping, and diagnostics.

b079d6fea545.source:
flowchart TD Y["Y | X ~ ExpFam( μ(X), φ )"] MU["μ(X) — modelled
g(μ(X)) = η(X) = f₁(x₁) + f₂(x₂) + ..."] PHI["φ (dispersion) — CONSTANT
not modelled"] SHAPE["shape, skewness
not in the model at all"] Y --> MU Y -.-> PHI PHI -.-> SHAPE
b079d6fea545.caption: A conventional GLM or GAM relates covariates to the conditional mean while treating dispersion as fixed or as determined by that mean.
b079d6fea545.alt: Conditional response distribution with a modeled mean predictor, constant dispersion, and no separate model for shape or skewness.

b29e70643adb.source:
flowchart TD OLS["OLS projection
hat matrix, degrees of freedom"] --> PLS["penalized least squares
ridge / difference penalty, λ ↔ df"] PLS --> SPL["P-splines / GAMs
base learners (bbs, bols, bmono)"] OLS --> GD["gradient descent
in parameter space"] GD --> BOOST["boosting = gradient descent
in function space, component-wise"] SPL --> BOOST BOOST --> GAMLSS["GAMLSS = multi-parameter
boosting"]
b29e70643adb.caption: Component-wise boosting connects projection and penalized smoothing with gradient descent in function space; distributional boosting extends the construction to multiple parameters.
b29e70643adb.alt: Conceptual progression from ordinary least squares and gradient descent through penalized smooth base learners and component-wise boosting to GAMLSS.

b7813ef0114a.source:
flowchart TD LOSS["1. THE LOSS (family) ρ(y, f)
Gaussian→mean, Binomial→prob,
Quantile→τ-quantile, Poisson→rate,
CoxPH→log-hazard, GAMLSS→dist. param"] LEARN["2. THE BASE LEARNERS g₁,...,gⱼ
bols(linear), bbs(spline),
bmono(monotone), bspatial(surface),
brandom(group), btree(tree)"] REG["3. THE REGULARIZATION (m_stop, ν)
m_stop chosen by cross-validation
ν=0.1 fixed; smaller ν → finer path"] LOSS -->|"determines negative gradient u"| LEARN LEARN -->|"each fit by penalized LS to u"| REG
b7813ef0114a.caption: Model-based boosting separates the loss, candidate base learners, and path regularization.
b7813ef0114a.alt: The family determines the negative gradient, structured base learners fit it by penalized least squares, and shrinkage plus early stopping regularize the path.

c80670d12baf.source:
flowchart LR U["negative gradient u"] --> L1["Fit ĝ₁ (bols on x₁)"] --> SSE1["SSE₁"] U --> L2["Fit ĝ₂ (bbs on x₂)"] --> SSE2["SSE₂ ⬅ WINNER"] U --> L3["Fit ĝ₃ (bmono on x₃)"] --> SSE3["SSE₃"] U --> LJ["Fit ĝⱼ (...)"] --> SSEJ["SSEⱼ"] SSE2 --> UPD["j* = argmin SSE
Update: f ← f + ν · ĝ₂"]
c80670d12baf.caption: Component-wise selection fits every candidate effect to the pseudo-residual and updates only the learner with minimum fitting error.
c80670d12baf.alt: Parallel candidate learner fits to the negative gradient produce SSE values; only the minimum-SSE learner contributes the next update.

cdbb14f4883b.source:
flowchart TD S0["Step 0: ŷ = ȳ
(just the mean)"] --> S1["Step 1: ŷ += ν·β̂₁·x₃
(x₃ best explains residual)"] S1 --> S2["Step 2: ŷ += ν·β̂₂·x₇
(x₇ best explains new residual)"] S2 --> S3["Step 3: ŷ += ν·β̂₃·x₃
(x₃ again — coefficient accumulates)"] S3 --> SN["..."]
cdbb14f4883b.caption: Forward stagewise regression builds the predictor through small updates to one selected component at a time.
cdbb14f4883b.alt: Successive forward-stagewise updates start from the response mean and repeatedly add a shrunken coefficient for the predictor that best explains the current residual.

e7ad66e0ea65.source:
flowchart LR
    Y["y — response vector"] --> HY["Hy = fitted values\n(closest point in C(X))"]
    Y --> RES["(I−H)y = residual\n(orthogonal to C(X))"]
    HY -.->|"the part X explains"| FIT["fitted model"]
    RES -.->|"the part X cannot explain"| NOISE["noise / unmodelled structure"]
e7ad66e0ea65.caption: The hat matrix decomposes the response into its projection onto the design space and an orthogonal residual.
e7ad66e0ea65.alt: Projection of the response vector into fitted values in the column space of the design matrix and a residual orthogonal to that space.

f2229555ec5d.source:
flowchart TD A["Phase 1 (small m): capturing SIGNAL
selected: x₃, x₇, x₁ (all in S)
risk decreases fast"] -->|CV picks m_stop here| B["Phase 2 (large m): fitting NOISE
selected: x₂, x₅, x₉ (NOT in S)
training risk ↓ slowly, test risk ↑"]
f2229555ec5d.caption: Early stopping truncates a stylized boosting path after the principal signal has been learned but before later noise-fitting updates dominate.
f2229555ec5d.alt: Two phases of a boosting path: early iterations select strong signal variables, whereas later iterations increasingly select noise variables.
